farewell: Mind the beavers on your way out.

reply: Dhira. The beavers call me something else, but you could not pronounce it.
I look after the beavers of Silvertides.
They are cleverer than most two-legs and they complain less.
Beautiful place, if you keep an eye out for parders and jungle moas.
Both grow out in the lagoon, and both have that silvery sheen now. Cut a sample with a knife and take it to the laboratory.
The refiner of magic in the laboratory here in Silvertides will tell you what is in those leaves.

walkaway: Mind the beavers on your way out.

greet: Greetings, two-leg. What a rare sight around here.

reply: Nilavarna, of the Silvertides.
I lead the nagas of these shores. The sea tells me what it wants and I listen.
Our home. Where the tide meets the stone and neither one wins.
The moon goddess. She fell once and the stars carried her back. We have not forgotten.
Our shaman. He hears the tides the way you hear voices.
She cares for the beavers and knows the plants of the lagoon better than any scholar.
She keeps the shop and works the yukti. If the magic is off, she noticed first.
The gestures that shape magic. Ask Nipuna, she lives by them.
Niral.
I keep the balance between the beast and the person here in Oskayaat.
He was one of us. Then he filled himself with moonsilver and stopped being anyone at all.
The moon goddess. We do not worship her the way the nagas do, but we respect what she can do.
The same runes that ended our uncontrolled were sickness. Drawn in blessed blue lava, they will silence the shard.
It runs in the old volcano on the eastern coast. Take a crystal flask and wear your moon mirror, or the heat will have you.
The beast can be controlled. The moon cannot. Never confuse the two.

farewell: May the Moon Goddess light your path.
greet: Greetings, traveller. May the Moon Goddess bless you.

reply: I am Saraki, maharani of Moonfall.
I rule Moonfall and I watch over the peace of my people.
Moonfall is where the goddess touched the world. We have guarded this place ever since.
The Moon Goddess fell upon this island long ago, and the stars themselves descended to carry her home.
Our astronomer. She sleeps by day and argues with the sky by night.
She keeps the potion shop here in Moonfall and knows the yukti better than anyone.
Our magic. Ask Sundara about it, she will explain it far better than I could.

walkaway: May the Moon Goddess light your path.

reply: Sharai.
I watch this stretch of coast. Lately it has been giving me plenty to watch.
An asura complex, drowned centuries ago. The sea took it slowly, wall by wall.
They claim the place now. Not all of them agree on what to do with it, which is the only good news.
They learned to live with the moon's darker face. If anyone can seal that shard, it is them.

farewell: May the tides always guide you safely.
greet: May the tides always guide you safely.

reply: Tarisu, shaman of Silvertides.
I listen to the sea and tell my people what it says.
The sea has one voice for every hour of the day. Lately one of them is a stranger.
The moon pulls the water. When the moon is troubled, so is the tide.
Three stones along the coast, set by my grandmother's grandmother. They have measured the water ever since.

walkaway: May the tides always guide you safely.

farewell: Mind the sky once in a while.

reply: Udu. Astronomer, insomniac, and the only one here who looks up.
I watch the sky above Marapur every night and write down what it does.
The stars are reliable. It is everything else that keeps surprising me.
East of Marapur, out where the water goes green. That is where it came down.
Whatever the priests say, something tore loose from her that night.

walkaway: Mind the sky once in a while.
